methodology: The study developed a novel bone-targeted nanoplatform using polymerization-induced self-assembly to synthesize bisphosphonate-functionalized copolymer nanoparticles of different morphologies (spherical, worm-like and vesicular). The properties were optimized by systematically varying the solid content and degree of polymerization.
research_objective: To develop a novel bone-targeted nanoplatform for delivering osteoporosis drugs using polymerization-induced self-assembly.

key_findings.finding: Novel bisphosphonate-functionalized copolymer nanoplatform developed for bone-targeted drug delivery
Polymer vesicles exhibit weak pH responsiveness, high loading capacity and sustained drug release properties.

Synthesis of PDMA30-NAS18 diblock copolymer and chain extension with DAAM via RAFT aqueous dispersion polymerization

Bisphosphonate- Block copolymer functionalized nanocarriers have been explored for bone-targeted drug delivery due to the affinity of Polymerization-inducted self-assembly bisphosphonates with Ca2+ , however, current targeted nanocarriers are mainly prepared by solvent switching, Vesicle which is cumbersome and unsustainable. Herein, we address the challenge by developing a novel bone-targeted Bone targetability drug delivery system using polymerization-induced self-assembly. We synthesized a bisphosphonate- functionalized acrylamide monomer and developed a series of polymer nanoparticles shaped with sphere, worm and vesicle by systematically varying polymer solid content and the degree of polymerization of diacetone acrylamide (DAAM). A detailed morphology phase diagram was constructed. The bisphosphonate-functionalized polymer vesicles exhibited weak pH responsive, high loading capacity for hydrophilic drug (up to 69 %), and sustained drug release (20 % drug release over 10 days). The bisphosphonate-func ctionalized polymer vesicles exhibited weak pH responsive, high loading capacity for hydrophilic drug (up to 69 %), and sustained drug release (20 % drug release over 10 days). The bisphosphonate-functionalized vesicles displayed a superior bone affinity in vitro (75 % bound in hydroxyapatite) and vivo (bonded in femur and spinal). These findings will support this bisphosphonate-functionalized nanoparticles as promising bone-targeted nanoplatform. 1.
